home.aboutMeDescription: I'm Zak, an Honours physics student at Concordia University, minoring in Science College, on track for a PhD in medical physics.
home.aboutMeDescription2: My current research explores symbolic self-projection, investigating how the spaces people imagine and the characters they identify with reflect ideal self-concept and psychological state. I'm developing this study independently, alongside my coursework, and I'm also currently working in a neuroscience lab investigating Drug Use Disorder in animal models.
home.aboutMeDescription3: I'm interested in the intersection of physics, psychology, and applied research methodology, with a long-term focus on medical imaging and physics applications in healthcare.
home.technologiesDescription: Throughout the development of my projects, I have become familiar with the following technologies:

projects.mainHeader: Here are some of the projects I've worked on! Click on a project to view its details.

physicsLibrary.infoPageDescription: An open-source Python library providing shared analysis and data-processing tools for my physics and neuroscience lab work. Built to keep core logic reusable across multiple lab GUIs and pipelines.

physicsAnalysisGui.infoPageDescription: A PyQt6 desktop application for loading, visualizing, and analyzing physics lab data, built on shared logic from PhysicsLibrary.

infoPageFeatureGroups.summary: Load TDT tank folders, Oxysoft/Artinis NIRS exports, Excel/CSV/TSV files, Terranova PT2 EFNMR/MRI images, and text-field study folders, all through one unified menu, with automatic detection of multiple side-by-side tables in a single sheet.

Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, and rectangle-select a region, with hover tracker dots that snap to the nearest line and show exact values. Switch between matplotlib and GPU-accelerated PyQtGraph rendering at any time, with golden-ratio font scaling that stays crisp through every resize.

Fit linear, exponential, Gaussian, or sinusoidal curves to any segment, run FFTs with automatic peak annotation, generate PETH / Z-score peri-event histograms for TDT recordings, and view PT2 EFNMR/MRI images with colormap selection and PNG/PDF/SVG export.

Bulk-add auto-detected markers by store or drop custom ones by hand, with high/low phase tracking for duration-based events. Rename or delete markers individually or in bulk, and measure the timing between every event with a sortable, exportable intervals table.

Compare any pair of fields across a folder of per-subject JSON data with no fixed schema, using sentence-transformer embeddings and paired similarity metrics. Full statistical validation follows: permutation testing, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, Cohen's d, word-count-controlled regression, bootstrap confidence intervals, and leave-one-out sensitivity checks.

neuroDataInterface.infoPageDescription: The first version of my data analysis GUI, originally built for Synapse TDT neuroscience data, supporting event marking, epoch analysis, and signal visualization for lab recordings. That work has since evolved into PhysicsAnalysisGUI, a general-purpose tool for all the data analysis and visualization I need across my research.

papers.introDescription: A selection of lab reports from my physics coursework. All plots and image reconstructions in these reports were generated with my own app, PhysicsAnalysisGUI.

efnmrMri.title: Earth's Field NMR and MRI of Biological Tissue
efnmrMri.description: Investigated Earth's field nuclear magnetic resonance and 2D spin-echo MRI using the Terranova system, measuring T1/T2 relaxation times in water and a bell pepper and imaging internal tissue structure at multiple resolutions.

nirsMuscle.title: Measuring Skeletal Muscle Oxygen Consumption with NIRS
nirsMuscle.description: Used near-infrared spectroscopy to track oxyhemoglobin and deoxyhemoglobin during venous and arterial occlusions at two exercise intensities, estimating forearm blood flow and tissue oxygen consumption from the hemoglobin signal slopes.
